The most common culprit is the **parent component re-rendering** — whenever the parent renders for any reason, React re-renders all its children unless you prevent it. If the parent creates new function references or object props on each render (like `<Child onClick={() => ...} />` or `<Child style={{...}} />`), the child sees new props and re-renders even if the values are the same.

The fix depends on what's causing it:

- **Wrap the child in `React.memo()`** — stops re-renders when props haven't actually changed.
- **Use `useCallback()` for functions** — keeps the same function reference across renders.
- **Move object/array props outside the component** or `useMemo()` them — so they don't get recreated each render.

If you share your code, I can point out exactly which one is happening.
